source.title: Visual Grounding Safety in Vision-Language Models
source.authors: Erfan Shayegani; Kundan Krishna; Yue Dong; Nael B. Abu-Ghazaleh; Leon A. Gatys; Shruti Palaskar

record.tranche_reason: The study compares reasoning-trace refusal with final grounding behavior, a different measure bearing on V5's proposed separation. It also analyzes a difference-in-means refusal direction, but does not causally intervene on that direction.
record.gate_note: The paper computes a refusal direction from harmful AdvBench and harmless Alpaca mean activations and measures projections onto it; it does not ablate or add the direction. Its fine-tuning results deliberately train refusal behavior and therefore are not evidence of naturally arising refusal. The system-prompt and training ablations concern output-form safety transfer, not the listed directional interventions.
record.test_reason: The study borrows the Arditi et al. difference-in-means direction (AdvBench minus Alpaca, last prompt token) as a fixed axis. It projects VLM activations onto it to show that fine-tuning moves harmful grounding requests toward the harmful centroid. It never ablates or adds the direction, never tests whether it mediates refusal, and never separates harm encoding from refusal internally. The behavioural results (VQA vs grounding refusal, trained refusal) concern output-form safety transfer and deliberately trained refusal. The VisionReasoner reasoning-trace vs answer split is a behavioural dissociation between two outputs, not an internal encoding of harmfulness separate from the refusal decision, so it does not test V5. It is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors conclude three things: grounding refusal trails VQA refusal by 31–59 points on average, and system prompts do not close the gap; grounding-form safety fine-tuning closes it while preserving capability; and projections onto an Arditi-style refusal direction show harmful requests moving toward it after fine-tuning, most for grounding. They also read the VisionReasoner trace/answer split as suggesting models can recognize harm without acting on it. They make no causal claim about the direction.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a harmful-minus-harmless mean activation direction and residual-stream projections, but applies this to VLM final prompt-token activations and does not perform the original causal ablation or addition.
record.method_sensitivity: The reasoning-trace/final-answer gap varies by domain; system-prompt condition and refusal-target fine-tuning also change reported behaviors, but do not test directional causality.

fits_no_version.finding: Across five VLMs, mean harmful refusal is far lower when the same request asks for a grounding than when it asks for a free-text answer: VLSU 19.4 vs 62.9, BBQ-V 16.7 vs 75.9, Asimov 12.7 vs 43.8.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal learned in text does not reliably transfer to a VLM's spatial grounding outputs.

fits_no_version.finding: VisionReasoner-7B's reasoning trace argues for refusal far more often than its final grounding answer refuses on BBQ-V (64.5% vs 0.6%). The gap is small on VLSU (12.5 vs 3.9) and absent on Asimov-2.0 (3.0 vs 3.0).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In reasoning VLMs, harm recognition in the reasoning trace can dissociate behaviourally from the final action, depending on domain.

fits_no_version.finding: Harmful grounding inputs project near the harmless centroid in base models. Safety fine-tuning shifts them toward the harmful centroid more than benign controls (e.g. VisionReasoner +0.42 harmful vs +0.07 benign).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Projection onto a text-derived refusal direction tracks behavioural refusal changes after safety fine-tuning in VLMs (correlational).

record.code_released: Will be released upon acceptance; URL not stated.
record.problems: No causal intervention on the refusal direction. The separate reasoning-trace diagnostic is available only for VisionReasoner; the refusal scoring relies on an LLM judge. Behavioral percentages have no reported confidence intervals or error bars, although representation figures show one-sigma bands.
record.rows_left_out: Not extracted: the full per-model harmful-refusal grid in Tables 6–7, system-prompt results, fine-tuned refusal rates, capability and over-refusal results, and per-category breakdowns. They address output-form safety, prompting, or deliberately trained refusal rather than a listed directional claim; the five-model mean modality comparison and the base VisionReasoner trace comparison are retained.

untested.parts: No ablation or addition of the direction. Projections are only correlational with behaviour, and there is no capability-preservation test tied to the direction.
No internal probe or direction separating harmfulness judgment from refusal. Only a behavioural trace/answer dissociation in VisionReasoner.
Applies a text-only reference direction to multimodal inputs without testing whether it transfers causally.
Fine-tuning shifts projections, but the study does not test whether training determines the existence of a removable direction.
VisionReasoner emits a reasoning trace, but no directional intervention is run on it.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 labels are dropped. The trace/answer comparison is behavioural, judged by Gemini, and available for only one model, so it does not measure separate internal encoding of harm and refusal. The direction is used purely as an analysis axis (T4).

versions.untested_parts: No ablation or addition of the difference-in-means direction; no test that it causally mediates refusal or preserves other abilities.
No weight-edit removal of the direction.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No comparison of a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account.
The paper compares reasoning-trace refusal with final grounding refusal for VisionReasoner, but does not directly identify separate internal encodings of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or shared-direction transfer test.
Training-form ablations affect refusal behavior and projections, but the study does not test whether training determines the existence of a causally removable direction.
No test of directional ablation or addition in reasoning models; the reasoning-trace diagnostic is not such a test.

rows.note: The trace more often argues for refusal than the final grounding answer, but the difference is modest.
rows.check: Reasoning-trace refusal (12.5%) vs final grounding refusal (3.9%) compares two behavioural outputs scored by an LLM judge. It does not measure whether harmfulness is encoded separately from the refusal decision (V5), so it should not link to V5. Values match Table 19 and Table 7.
